PE and Sport Premium
PE and Sport Premium
What is the PE and Sport Premium Funding?
In March 2013, the Government announced it was providing funding of £150 million per year to improve the provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools in England. It supports schools to provide sustainable improvements to the quality of their physical education, sport and activity programmes.
At Marchwood C of E Infant School we use the PE and Sport Premium Funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of Physical Education, School Sport and Physical Activity (PESSPA) we offer. We use the Primary PE and Sport Premium to develop or add to the PESSPA activities (Physical Education, School Sport and Physical Activity) that our school already offer and to build capacity and capability within our school to ensure that improvements made now will benefit pupils joining the school in future years.
How is the money being spent?
Schools must publish the amount of Primary PE and sport premium received for the academic year; a full breakdown of how it has been spent; what impact the school has seen on pupils’ Physical Education, School Sport and Physical Activity, participation and attainment and how the improvements will be sustainable in the future.
Please see the report below which provides details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values | Marchwood Church of England Infant School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Vision and Values
Vision Statement
We want our children to love learning, love each other, and care for God’s world, just as God asked people to look after His creation.
Through all of this, we help every child grow and flourish, living the joyful “life in all its fullness” that Jesus promised.
Values
Our core Christian values of Love, Courage and Hope, are the foundations of our vision and underpin the Christian distinctiveness of our school. By developing a deep understanding of these values, children will develop the character traits that enable them to flourish and be inspired and motivated to make a positive difference in the world.
These include understanding how to build positive relationships with each other, having the courage to stand up for what is right, the knowledge to make good choices and the ability to respect and embrace one another’s differences.
We also recognise that these values are not exclusively Christian and are accepted by people of all faiths or no faith at all. Although these values may be supported and shared by Christians and non-Christians alike, children are helped to understand what is distinctively Christian about each value through key bible stories alongside other stories that exemplify the values. These show us examples of how Christians live their life and the lessons we can learn from Jesus. Children and staff constantly refer to the values in everyday life and by ensuring our values are the cornerstone of life in school, our children are helped to understand how the Christian values of Love, Courage and Hope can be applied to their own lives.
Threaded throughout our values and school life is our inclusive practise
Love: Inclusion is an act of love — making sure every child feels seen, valued, and safe.
Courage: Inclusion requires courage — to challenge what is false, to speak up, and to change.
Hope: Inclusion is built on hope — the belief that every child can thrive and contribute meaningfully
The school's Terms of Union with the National Society
Our Church School has been in Marchwood since it's foundation in 1854.The school has a Terms of Union with the National Society, which gives direction to our school vision for education. This document is displayed in the main school entrance. Please find a copy of this below.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium is additional funding allocated to schools to support disadvantaged pupils and help overcome challenges they may face, including those arising from deprivation in order to improve education outcomes. These include pupils whose families are on a low income and are entitled to free school meals (FSM) and those looked after by the local authority (LAC).
A premium has also been introduced for children of armed service personnel (Service Children In Education - SCiE). This service premium is designed to support the emotional and social wellbeing of these pupils.
All schools are required to report on the amount of funding received and how this is being used. Once information is available, the impact of the funding should also be reported.
Pupil Premium
Eligibility
If your child is eligible for pupil premium free school meals, the school will receive additional money under the 'Pupil Premium' funding. To find out if your child is eligible, please follow the link https://www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/freeschoolmeals/juniorsecondary and click on "check to see if you are eligible for free school meals". This is a very simple process; you will need your national insurance number and date of birth and you will be given an instant response.

Ofsted
Our most recent Ofsted was in April 2023. The inspection focused on confirming whether the school remained good and we are delighted to confirm this judgement was upheld. The inspection particularly noted our caring community, broad and ambitious curriculum and the very clear system that supports behaviour. Please find our latest report below.
SIAMS
All Church of England schools receive a Section 48 Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) as well as Ofsted inspections.
A SIAMS inspection focuses on the impact of the Church school’s Christian vision on pupils and adults. This involves looking at the school’s Christian vision, the provision the school makes because of this vision and, crucially, how effective this provision is in enabling all pupils to flourish.
Our last SIAMS inspection was in 2019, when we were graded 'Excellent'. Please find the report below.
